articles.title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
articles.excerpt: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is built so thousands of agents can push to a single repository at once. Here's how it works. The post Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand.

Through internal testing, we've demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency.
This new architecture is the foundation for GitHub to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers, and we've been building it underneath GitHub while it keeps running.
Over the past year, agents changed what a busy repository looks like on GitHub.
In our first post in this series, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation Git storage architecture: minimize coordination, and decouple storage from compute.

articles.title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
articles.excerpt: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.
details: It may be indistinguishable from a human user carrying out a task, or it might look like one visitor carrying many Users.
This removes the ability for the Site to recognize, serve, and hold accountable the user or users behind the Agent, and causes the Site to face the costs when something goes wrong.
This post argues that in order for Sites to maximize the access they provide to Agents, the ecosystem must develop new mechanisms to preserve the relationship between Sites and Users.

Traditionally, in Security and Fraud Prevention, that requires three things: Identity, Reputation, and Accountability, allowing Sites to answer: Is the person acting being truthful about who they are?
“Personal AI Agents” (“Agents” for short) are automations that take instructions from a human (“User”) and pursue a goal by controlling a cloud computer or browser.

articles.title: Cult.fit builds operational muscle with Codex
articles.excerpt: Cult.fit is using Codex to help teams across functions build tools, move faster, and change how work gets done.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/cultfit-builds-with-codex/ Cult.fit is one of India’s leading technology-enabled fitness companies, operating 708 fitness centers across 77 cities and serving nearly one million paid members.

Its business combines subscription-based access to gyms and trainer-led fitness classes with a growing consumer products portfolio spanning fitness equipment, accessories, workout footwear and activewear.
As the company grew, it wanted to solve more operational and product challenges without adding layers of process and complexity.
By standardizing engineering on Codex and then extending it beyond engineering, cult.fit is helping teams across the organization analyze data, build tools, and move ideas into production.
Alongside its Codex rollout, it is using the OpenAI API to develop more personalized member experiences, including through its AI Trainer.

articles.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
articles.excerpt: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
details: When I last wrote about our DNS propagation pipeline in 2022 , the Zone Builder received about 250 DNS record changes per second.
Today it receives about 700, nearly three times as many, plus about 100 other events, such as zone setting changes.
However, the number of events was never the real problem.
The problem was the kind of work some of those events needed, and how that work grows with the size of a zone.
Some zones now hold more than 20 million records, and we expect them to keep growing toward hundreds of millions.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.excerpt: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.
details: Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection . Your origin stays private, while web application firewall ( WAF ), caching , bot management , and Workers work just as they do for public origins.

In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet.
Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.

Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.

articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.
details: Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report.
This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 - July, August, and September - and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume.

The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One , Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network .
Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%.

Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year.

articles.title: Docker and ActiveState Extending Secure Defaults to the Packages Developers Install
articles.excerpt: Docker partners with ActiveState to continue to provide one standard for trusted content across everything you and your teams build on.
details: Trusted content is the foundation security-conscious organizations expect all builds to start from.
Docker has made that possible for everyone by providing the foundation free.
Docker Hardened Images (DHI) are open source under Apache 2.0, with a catalog of 4,000+ minimal images (and growing) built from source and continuously maintained by Docker.
The catalog also carries customizable Helm charts and over 65,000 hardened system packages.
For most services, adopting DHI is as simple as changing the FROM line.

articles.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
articles.excerpt: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, OpenAI’s cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes, trained to stay within authorized scope.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-cyber/ We’re introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, a major leap in security research: more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set.

GPT‑6 Cyber delivers major gains on key cybersecurity benchmarks over GPT‑5.6 Cyber, including a 51% relative improvement on ExploitGym and a step function improvement when tested on staying within scope.
It is already helping to secure real-world software, uncovering and validating thousands of exploits in security-critical codebases such as Linux and Firefox.
On ExploitGym, which tests whether models can exploit a specified vulnerability, GPT‑6 Cyber scores 48.5%, up from 32.1% for GPT‑5.6 Cyber.

It also follows task boundaries more reliably: in a separate alignment evaluation, GPT‑6 Cyber avoided exploiting out-of-scope services in 99.93% of tests without its deployment prompt, and 100% with this prompt.

articles.title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
articles.excerpt: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.
details: You receive a ping: a new critical vulnerability has been disclosed.

Your team scrambles to compare vendor advisories, read technical research, check which systems run the affected software, and answer familiar questions from the business: are we affected, and what are we doing about it?
Another disclosure arrives before that work is finished.

AI is changing both the volume and speed of critical vulnerability discovery. It can analyze large codebases at scale and surface deeply nested flaws that may have existed for years without being found through human review. That discovery momentum will put more pressure on security teams to understand the impact of each disclosure on their infrastructure.

To help security teams prepare, today we’re introducing Zero Wire : a public vulnerability intelligence feed on Cloudflare Radar, bringing the clarity of a news wire service to critical security developments. It helps security leaders and practitioners understand significant vulnerabilities and decide what to do next.

articles.title: CNCF Score project improved its security posture by joining the Docker-Sponsored Open Source Program
articles.excerpt: See how CNCF Score improved container security with Docker Scout, Hardened Images, and the Docker-Sponsored Open Source Program.
details: Score, a CNCF Sandbox project, recently joined the Docker-Sponsored Open Source (DSOS) Program to strengthen the security of its container images and release pipeline.

In this post, the Score maintainers share what we adopted (Docker Hub, Docker Scout, Docker Hardened Images, the Docker GitHub Builder, and OIDC connections), the results we measured, and how other open source projects, within the CNCF and beyond, can apply the same practices by default.

In September 2025, the CNCF announced a partnership with Docker to expand infrastructure support for project maintainers through the Docker-Sponsored Open Source (DSOS) Program. The partnership gives CNCF projects access to Docker’s security scanning tools, container registry, and best-practice resources at no cost.
This aligned closely with the discussions held at the Maintainer Summit NA 2025 in Atlanta , which centered on increasing collaboration across CNCF projects and demonstrating security best practices.
The Docker-Sponsored Open Source (DSOS) Program supports non-commercial open source projects with Docker tooling and infrastructure.

articles.title: Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub
articles.excerpt: GitHub now highlights ACCESSIBILITY.md files and helps maintainers document accessibility goals, known barriers, supported environments, contributor expectations, and reporting processes. The post Accessibility statements now have a home on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Accessibility work often lives in issue trackers, contribution guidelines, audit reports, team knowledge, and conversations with users. When that information has no predictable home, people who encounter a barrier must search for it, and maintainers lose context as contributors and project ownership change.

An ACCESSIBILITY.md file, now visible on repository overview pages, gives a project one durable place to explain its accessibility goals, contributor expectations, supported environments, known limitations, and process for reporting barriers.

GitHub now recognizes the ACCESSIBILITY.md file in the repository's root, .github/ directory, or docs/ directory. A repository can also inherit a statement from its organization's .github/ repository. For public repositories, maintainers can add or propose a statement from Insights > Community Standards using a concise starter document.
GitHub's community health files help people understand how a project works:
Codes of conduct establish expectations for participation

articles.title: Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world
articles.excerpt: Louis Erbkamm built the first prototype in his free time. Now GitHub Copilot helps him maintain it alone. The post Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Louis Erbkamm knows his way around Arnis, the smallest town in Germany, but he's never set foot in it.
I know where the shops are. Where the boats are... I know the city pretty well, but I haven't been there yet.

Arnis is also the name of his open source project, which takes real-world data from OpenStreetMap and other sources to turn places you know into Minecraft worlds you can freely explore. Since Louis started Arnis in 2022, it's reached close to 900,000 downloads from GitHub and about 70 contributors.

Louis grew up playing Minecraft and started coding at 13, always looking for ways to bring code into the game. Arnis began as a fun diversion combining Minecraft with geospatial data, and it went on GitHub, where he already kept his side projects. He finished the first prototype within two weeks while on a break from school.

That first version was Python written by hand, built only on OpenStreetMap, and generating a town took a while. He needed somewhere real to test it, so he looked up towns in Germany, where he lives, and found Arnis. A small town helped while early generation was slow.

articles.title: Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT
articles.excerpt: GitHub’s annual month-long game jam is back for its 14th year! This November, make a game inspired by the theme SHIFT. Change gears, swap perspectives, bend reality, or just press a certain key. The post Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Game Off , GitHub's annual month-long game jam, returns for its 14th year this November. Thousands of developers have joined us over the years to make everything from polished platformers to wonderfully weird experiments.
Whether you're making your first game or your fiftieth, we'd love for you to join us.
Shift gears. Shift perspectives. Shift dimensions. Shift bits. Work the night shift. Or make a game where the only buttons are the Shift keys.
You have until December 1, 2026, at 13:37 PST to build and submit a game inspired by SHIFT. Strong or loose inspirations apply!
A change in position, direction, perspective, or reality.
